title: Identified-Set Geometry of Distributional Model Extraction under Top-K Censored API Access
claim: Even with generous top-K access, the set of compatible solutions stays large, so recovery is fundamentally limited.
layout: 1 panel, dual y-axes, log-like x-axis, shaded variability band, dotted reference line
description: A single line plot with a shared x-axis of censoring threshold K (5 to 100) and two y-axes. The left axis, in blue, shows the total-variation diameter U_K. Its solid line with circle markers falls from about 0.98 to 0.81, and a light blue band shows ±1 s.d. over prompts. The right axis, in red, shows the KL lower bound R_bin. Its dashed line with square markers falls from about 0.65 to 0.44. A dotted horizontal gray line is labeled 'typical API (K=20)'. A legend sits at lower left. The eye goes first to the blue curve and shaded band at the top. Both curves decline slowly and stay high, so the plot argues that ambiguity persists even at large K.
caption: TV diameter $\Uk$ and binary endpoint KL lower bound $R_{\mathrm{bin}}$ as a function of $K$ on Qwen3-0.6B math teacher (shading: $\pm 1$ population s.d.\ over 3{,}200 prompts). Even at $K{=}100$, $\Uk > 0.80$ and $R_{\mathrm{bin}} > 0.43$: the vast majority of the distribution remains unresolved.
abstract: Modern LLM APIs often reveal only top-$K$ logit scores and censor the remaining vocabulary. We study the per-position distribution-recovery limits of this access model. For censoring threshold $Ï$, the compatible teacher distributions form an identified set whose total-variation diameter is exactly $U_K=(V-K)\exp(Ï)/(Z_A+(V-K)\exp(Ï))$, where $Z_A$ is the observed partition function. For KL recovery, we give a computable binary-endpoint lower bound and an asymptotically matching small-ambiguity upper bound, with an extension to reference-aware attackers. Experiments on a Qwen3 math-reasoning teacher reveal a layered extraction hierarchy: on-task top-$K$ distillation recovers 12% of private capability, full-logit distillation recovers 56% despite 99% KL closure, and generation-based extraction recovers 96%. Top-$K$ censoring therefore limits per-position distribution recovery but does not by itself prevent capability extraction, separating fidelity from transfer in prompt-only logit distillation.
